answer: An agent market can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may submit bids, with the stake recorded at a registry vertex and tied to a signed cipher of its public key. A random, rate-limited inlet assigns work only to staked keys; when a key is caught submitting duplicate claims or colluding, its stake is slashed after a challenge period. Creating many fake identities therefore requires buying and immobilizing real capital, while detectable abuse risks losing it—not merely generating more names.
